| `web.notion_redirect_uri` | Redirect URI of the Notion sign-in (7.2.5); must be entered exactly like this in the public Notion connection. HTTPS or localhost, path `/auth/notion/callback`. Default `http://localhost:8765/auth/notion/callback`. | File |
title: Paths, Logs and Web Server

text:
From 8.1, enter your mailbox email address, select a provider or use automatic
detection and choose **Load provider settings**. This only loads local defaults;
it neither connects nor saves the mailbox. Server settings remain editable.
Gmail and Microsoft mailbox OAuth require a separate grant and prior operator
registration. Choose **Connect Google mailbox** or **Connect Microsoft mailbox**,
check the available folders and explicitly adopt the connection. Calendar grants
do not authorize mailbox access.

Verified for Mailhelp 8.1. This guide leads from an empty directory to the first
checked suggestion. It applies to Windows 11 and Linux; deviations for Docker are marked.

**Goal:** Mailhelp is running, is reachable in the browser, reads a mailbox, has an AI connection
and knows Calendar and task list. An external entry occurs only after your
explicit confirmation.
title: Initial setup

text:
- Python 3.12 (Windows: `py -3.12`, Linux: `python3.12`) or Docker with Compose.
- Credentials of an IMAP mailbox (server, port, username, password or app password).
- A key for OpenRouter **or** a locally running Ollama server.
- Optional: access to Google Calendar/Todoist, Outlook/Microsoft To Do or a
  CalDAV server; optionally a Telegram bot with your user and chat ID.
title: Prerequisites

text:
**Windows 11** (PowerShell in the Mailhelp directory):

```powershell
py -3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements.lock
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install --no-deps -e .
```

**Linux:**

```sh
python3.12 -m venv .venv
.venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.lock
.venv/bin/python -m pip install --no-deps -e .
```

**Docker:** no installation necessary; continue with Stage 2.
title: 1. Install

path: 2. Start and read the terminal code
text:
Without `config.yaml`, Mailhelp starts the protected setup assistant.

- Windows: `.venv\Scripts\mailhelp --config-directory .`
- Linux: `.venv/bin/mailhelp --config-directory .`
- Docker: `docker compose -f compose.setup.yaml up --build`

**Result:** The terminal shows a one-time code and the address `http://localhost:8765`.
If the code is missing, request a new one with `mailhelp --pair --config-directory .` (Docker:
`docker compose exec mailhelp mailhelp --pair --config-directory /config`).
title: 2. Start and read the terminal code

text:
1. Open `http://localhost:8765/einrichtung/start`.
2. Enter the code in **Code from the Mailhelp console** and select **Pair device**.

**Result:** The page “Set up Mailhelp: Web access and time zone” appears (Stage 1 of 5).
title: 3. Pair in the browser

text:
Each stage has **Check** and **Save and continue**; via the stage list you can go back at any time. **Check** tests the entered values and saves nothing. The result appears above the form: for a problem, cause, affected field (with link to it), and concrete steps for resolution. The entered values remain, passwords are never displayed again. Password fields remain displayed empty: **Empty: keep saved value**. At most ten checks per minute are possible to avoid account locks at the email provider.

1. **Web access and time zone:** Check **Time zone** (e.g. `Europe/Berlin`) and set a **Web password (at least 12 characters)**.
2. **Mailbox:** Enter **IMAP server**, **Port**, **Encryption** (`ssl` usually port 993, `starttls` usually 143), username (`IMAP_USERNAME`), and password (`IMAP_PASSWORD`) and select **Check**. Then select **Inbox** and **Drafts folder** from the found folder list.
3. **AI provider:** `openrouter` with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` or `ollama` with **Ollama address (HOST:PORT)**; select **Check**.
4. **Calendar and Tasks:** Select **Calendar service** and **Task service** and enter the matching identifier (**Google Calendar ID**, **Todoist project ID**, **CalDAV calendar address**, **CalDAV task address**, **Outlook Calendar ID**, **Microsoft To Do list**). For Google and Microsoft, **Connect Google** and **Connect Microsoft** are available respectively. Details: [Settings, Targets section](Web-Einstellungen.md#ziele).
5. **Completion:** **Check all** shows every stage with ✓ or ✗ and a link to it. Check **Save configuration and start normal operation** and select **Save and start**. If a check fails, the same overview appears and nothing is activated.

**Result:** “Setup completed”. `config.yaml` and `.env` are saved; the credentials are only in `.env`.
title: 4. Run through wizard

text:
1. Open `http://localhost:8765/anmelden` and sign in with the web password. You pair additional devices with **Send code via Telegram** (when Telegram is active) or a new terminal code.
2. Open **Settings → Check connections**: The checks only read and change nothing.
3. Under **Status** you see the last contact per service; the mailbox appears after the first email retrieval.
title: 5. Sign In and Check Connections

text: In **Settings**, each setting shows “active” or “saved – takes effect only after a restart” or “… at the next safe point”. Restart: **Settings → Restart Mailhelp**.
title: 6. Recognize Saved and Active State

text:
1. Send an email with a clear request to yourself, e.g., “Please send the form back by Friday.”
2. After the next retrieval, a suggestion with Evidence appears under **Open**.
3. Select **Add as task** (for Events, **Add to calendar**). Mailhelp first reports “Saved – the entry will be verified with the provider” and after the verification retrieval “Created and verified”.

For a run without a real entry, set `test_mode: true`: confirmations are then only simulated.
title: 7. First Test Case

text:
| Message or situation | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| “Mailhelp is already running …” | Quit the running instance via **Settings → Quit Mailhelp** or with Ctrl+C |
| Code expired or forgotten | `mailhelp --pair --config-directory .` |
| Mailbox check fails | The message above the form states the cause and field; see the table below |
| Web password forgotten | On the computer `mailhelp --reset-web-password --config-directory .` |
| Docker: file permissions under Linux | `mkdir -p data logs` and `sudo chown 65532:65532 data logs` |
title: If something does not work

text:
**Check** states the cause, the affected field, and concrete steps for a problem. The
most common cases:

| Message | What usually helps |
| --- | --- |
| The IMAP server is not known under this name. | Check the spelling, enter only the server name without `https://` |
| The IMAP server does not respond on this port. | Port 993 with `ssl` or 143 with `starttls`; check firewall |
| Port and encryption do not match. | 993 belongs to `ssl`, 143 to `starttls` |
| The server rejected the login. | Full email address as username; for two-factor authentication an app password; enable IMAP in webmail |
| The specified inbox was not found. | Select one of the mentioned folders, usually `INBOX` |
| OpenRouter did not accept the key. | Copy the key completely (starts with `sk-or-`) |
| No credit or limit remains for this key. | Top up credit or increase limit |
| Ollama does not respond at this address. | Start `ollama serve`; from Docker `http://host.docker.internal:11434` |
| The Google authorization has expired or was revoked. | Run **Connect Google** again (required after 7 days in the Google app's test mode) |
| The Google Calendar API is disabled for the Google project. | Enable the Calendar API in the Google Cloud Console |
| Calendar, list, or project was not found. | Select calendar or check Todoist project ID |
| Too many checks in a short time. | Wait one minute (protection against account blocks at the email provider) |

Next: [Manage accounts](Konten-verwalten.md), [Settings](Web-Einstellungen.md).
title: Common messages during Check (from 6.1)

text:
From 8.1, the add-mailbox form offers the same local provider defaults as initial
setup. Custom domains can be assigned to a hosting provider explicitly; manual
setup remains available. Gmail/Microsoft mailbox OAuth needs operator registration
and a separate grant. New readers replace the affected mailbox between mail cycles;
a failed connection keeps the previous reader and leaves other mailboxes unchanged.

Verified for Mailhelp 8.1. Add, change and remove additional mailboxes, IServ accounts and additional Calendar/Task targets in an already set up installation.

**Principle:** Credentials are stored only in `.env` and are maintained under **Settings → Credentials**; only “stored” or “missing” is displayed. Changes to mailboxes and targets are drafts and are only applied after a renewed explicit confirmation. None of these pages creates Tasks or Events.
title: Manage accounts

text:
**Prerequisite:** Server, port, connection type and credentials of the mailbox.

1. Open **Settings → Mailboxes** and select **Add mailbox**.
2. Fill in:
   - **Display name**, e.g. “School”.
   - **IMAP server** and **Port**.
   - **Connection type**: **SSL/TLS (usually port 993)**, **STARTTLS (usually port 143)** or
     **Unencrypted (only in your own network)**.
   - **Username (usually the full email address)** and **Password or app password**.
   - **Folders (comma-separated, the first is the inbox)** and **Folder for
     reply drafts**.
   - **Do not process older mails before (empty: all existing mails)**, pre-filled with today.
3. Select **Check connection and activate mailbox**.

**Result:** After successful verification of login, folder list and read access, `config.yaml` and `.env` are saved (`IMAP_<n>_USERNAME`/`IMAP_<n>_PASSWORD`). The new mailbox is added between two mail cycles, without restart. If the check fails, all entries except the password are retained; the message names the cause without server response. Duplicate accounts are rejected. If you do not want to activate immediately, select **Instead, add as draft only**.
title: Add another mailbox

path: Assign a mailbox to another calendar or another task list
text:
1. Under **Settings → Target profiles**, use **Add target profile** to create a profile
   (name, calendar service, task service and the respective identifiers) – see
   “Other targets” below.
2. **Settings → Mailboxes**, open the mailbox, tab **Targets**, set **Target profile** to the
   new profile.
3. **Review draft** and then confirm **Take draft**.

**Result:** New proposals of this mailbox go to the new target. Already existing
proposals remain bound to their previous target; for the new target a new confirmation is
required.
title: Assign a mailbox to another calendar or another task list

text:
On the mailbox page there are the tabs **Goals**, **Filters**, **Topics**, **Replies** and
**Notifications**. Unset fields inherit the global setting; Reset
removes the local rule. Examples: custom default durations for events, custom signature for
reply drafts, shorter retention, custom quiet hours, local sender blocks or
exceptions from global blocks. All fields: [Settings](Web-Einstellungen.md#postfächer-imapmailboxes).
title: Rules per Mailbox

text:
1. Open **Settings → IServ accounts**.
2. Under **Activate directly**, enter display name, Address of the school (a copied IServ link is shortened to the school address), the Mailbox whose target profile and standards apply, optionally a start limit, as well as username and password. Empty access fields use already stored values (`ISERV_<n>_USERNAME`/`ISERV_<n>_PASSWORD`).
3. Select **Check connection and activate account**.

**Result:** Only after successful login are the account and access data saved. Retrieval starts without a restart in the next secure mail cycle; if applicable, answer open queries first. Parent letters always count as relevant. Anyone who does not want to activate immediately selects **Add IServ account as draft**.
title: Add IServ account

text:
Profile 1 is the target from the initial setup (**Edit default profile 1**). Additional profiles
(number 2–99) under **Settings → Target profiles**:

1. **Add target profile**, choose designation, calendar service (Google, CalDAV, Outlook) and
   task service (Todoist, Microsoft To Do, CalDAV, Apple Reminders).
2. Enter the identifiers; for Google or Microsoft, sign in via **Connect Google** or
   **Connect Microsoft** and for Google **Select Google Calendar** or
   **Select Google Tasks list**. The target selection is saved as a setup draft.
3. **Check accesses**: The diagnostic only reads and creates nothing.
4. Check the draft and take it.
title: Additional targets (Calendars and task lists)

text:
| Task | Path | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Change mailbox setting | Mailbox page, select tab, **Review draft**, **Take draft** | between mail cycles or after restart |
| Remove mailbox | Mailbox page, **Remove mailbox**, confirm | is removed from the configuration; no longer retrieved after restart |
| Temporarily switch off mailbox | in `config.yaml` `enabled: false` for the mailbox | after restart |
| Remove target profile | Target profile page, **Remove profile** | only possible when no mailbox uses it anymore (“Used by: …”) |
| Change, deactivate, or remove IServ account | IServ page; the change is saved as a draft | after explicit taking of the draft and restart |
| Renew credentials | **Settings → Credentials** | Diagnostics immediately, email retrieval after restart |
title: Change, deactivate, and remove

text:
For a rejected mailbox OAuth sign-in, “Reconnect mailbox” in the warning opens the
affected Google or Microsoft mailbox. Restart the flow after a configuration or
credential change. For iCloud, start with the suggested name before `@`; if sign-in
fails, try the full iCloud address as described in Apple's instructions.

| Situation | Next Stage |
| --- | --- |
| “There are already … Mailboxes set up.” | Remove or change an existing Mailbox |
| Check reports incorrect login credentials | Username is usually the full Address; with two-factor protection use an app password |
| Folder missing | Enter the folder name exactly as the server reports it; the check shows the found list |
| Target unreachable | **Check access**; for Google or Microsoft, renew the sign-in |
| Target profile cannot be removed | First assign Mailboxes listed under “Used by” to another profile |
title: If something does not work

text:
Hosted Inboxstride instances use **Connect with Google**, then select a calendar
with write access and explicitly **Adopt connection**. The operator manages client
credentials centrally. Changing only the calendar uses the existing grant;
disconnecting stops token issuance without deleting events. Mailbox access requires
its own grant. The direct self-hosted calendar setup below remains supported.

Verified for Mailhelp 8.1; provider documentation compared on 11 and 16 November 2026. A **target profile** determines into which calendar and which task list
confirmed proposals of a mailbox are entered. Profile 1 is the `targets` section
from initial setup; additional profiles are managed in **Settings → Target profiles**. An
**account** is the access at the provider (credentials in `.env`), the calendar or
list ID the specific target within this account.

Mailhelp writes only after your explicit confirmation of exactly the displayed
proposal version and then checks each entry with a fresh retrieval.
Created entries can be removed again within the deadline (by default 10 minutes, `targets.removal_window_minutes`)
via web or Telegram, provided the target allows safe removal:
Google Calendar, Outlook, Todoist and CalDAV calendars. For Microsoft To Do, CalDAV tasks,
Apple Reminders and Google Tasks, Mailhelp does not offer removal; even a direct command is
rejected. Please edit such entries at the provider.
title: Connect Calendar and Tasks

text:
| Provider | Role | Access (`.env`) | Identifier | What is checked | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Google Calendar | Calendar | `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN` | Calendar ID or `primary` | Title, times, all-day, location, description | Redirect URI must be entered in the Google Console |
| Todoist | Tasks | `TODOIST_TOKEN` | Project ID | Title, description, due date, project | Changes and cancellations only for events |
| Outlook | Calendar | `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID`, optional `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET`, sign-in via device code | Calendar or `default` | like Google | Cancellations delete the event |
| Microsoft To Do | Tasks | like Outlook | List or `default` ("Tasks") | Title, description, due date day | only day-accurate, no time |
| Notion (7.2) | Tasks | `NOTION_TOKEN` (internal connection) | Data source ID and property IDs | Title, description, deadline | without a status field, no detection of done pages; no removal |
| Google Tasks (7.2) | Tasks | like Google Calendar; sign-in with Google Tasks permission | List ID or `@default` (first list) | Title, notes, due date day | only day-accurate; an exact deadline is in the text; no removal |
| CalDAV | Calendar and Tasks | `CALDAV_USERNAME`, `CALDAV_PASSWORD` (app password) | Address of the collection | Resource with UID, fields, status | Recurring events are never changed |
| Apple Reminders | Tasks (via CalDAV) | like CalDAV (iCloud app password) | Address of the list | like CalDAV | lists switched to new iCloud reminders are not reachable via CalDAV |
| Calendar file | Calendar (via Telegram) | – | – | not checkable | whether the file was imported, Mailhelp cannot know |
title: Providers and their capabilities

text:
1. Under **Settings → Credentials**, store the Client ID and Client Secret of the
   web application client; the **Google redirect URI (web application client)**
   must be entered in the Google Cloud Console.
2. Select **Connect Google**, consent in the Google window, and **Complete Google sign-in**.
3. **Select Google Calendar** and take the desired calendar.
4. **Check accesses**.

Alternatively without a web application client: [Google: OAuth Playground guide](../Google-OAuth-Playground.md).

For an external Google project with publishing status “Testing”, the refresh token
can expire after seven days. Then renew the sign-in and check the project status.
title: Google Calendar

text:
1. In the Google project, enable the **Google Tasks API**. If it is off, **Check access**
   reports exactly that.
2. Select `google_tasks` as the task service and enter the **Google Tasks list** (`@default`
   for the first list of the account or the ID of a list).
3. Run **Connect Google** again: the sign-in now additionally requests the permission for
   Google Tasks (`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/tasks`). Already granted Calendar permissions remain.
   On a computer, this also works with `mailhelp --google-auth --config-directory .`; the
   sign-in requests exactly the permissions that the profile uses.
4. Open **Select Google Tasks list** in the setup or in the target profile, select the desired
   existing list and **Save as draft**. Mailhelp reads all available pages.
   On a read error, the selection is aborted.
5. Review the setup draft, **Check access**, and take the Settings.

The list selection creates a versioned draft. The first Task then requires the explicit confirmation of its suggestion version. Preview and Telegram show “Google Tasks adopts the Date; the exact Deadline is in the text.”.

Google Tasks stores only a day for a Task, no time. Mailhelp enters the confirmed day in the configured time zone and additionally writes an exact Deadline into the text, for example `Deadline: 2026-05-12, 18:00 (Europe/Berlin)`. There is no time-exact reminder from Google for this. Without a Deadline, the Date remains empty.
title: Google Tasks

text:
Mailhelp creates a page in a Notion data source for each confirmed task. You set up the table yourself; Mailhelp does not create data sources or properties.

1. In Notion, create a database with these properties: Title, Description (Text), Deadline (Date), Source (URL), Process (Text), and optionally Status (Status, Select, or Checkbox).
2. In Notion, create an internal connection with the capabilities Read content and Insert content, and share the database with this connection.
3. Store the token as `NOTION_TOKEN` (additional profiles: `NOTION_2_TOKEN`, etc.). Alternatively, a public connection: store `NOTION_CLIENT_ID` and `NOTION_CLIENT_SECRET`, enter the redirect URI `web.notion_redirect_uri` in Notion, and under **Settings → Target profiles** select **Connect Notion**. Mailhelp stores the rotating tokens in `notion-token.json` next to `.env` and remains bound to the selected workspace.
4. Under **Settings → Target profiles**, select **Select Notion data source**; the data sources shared for the connection are displayed. Then **Map Notion properties**: for each field, a property of the matching type and optionally the status field with the option for new pages and the options that count as done. Both are saved as a draft and applied like any settings change. Then set the task service to Notion. Alternatively, the IDs can be entered directly in `config.yaml` (see `config.example.yaml`).
5. **Check access**: Mailhelp reads the schema and reports a missing property or an incorrect type. Mailhelp does not create a test page.

If a property is later missing or its type changes, Mailhelp blocks new creations until the mapping is correct again; it is also checked directly before each creation. Without a status field, Mailhelp cannot recognize done Notion tasks.
title: Notion

text:
1. Store the API token from the Todoist settings under **Settings → Credentials** as
   `TODOIST_TOKEN`.
2. Enter the **Todoist project ID** (from the project address in the browser).
3. **Check access**.
title: Todoist

text:
1. Store `MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID` (app registration with “Allow public client flows”).
2. **Connect Microsoft**, **Start sign-in**, take the displayed code with **Copy code** and enter it at Microsoft. On the computer, this also works with
   `mailhelp --microsoft-login --config-directory .`.
3. Enter the **Outlook Calendar ID** or the **Microsoft To Do list** (`default` for the
   default calendar or the “Tasks” list) and **Check access**.
title: Outlook and Microsoft To Do

text:
1. Store `CALDAV_USERNAME` and `CALDAV_PASSWORD`; for iCloud, use an app password.
2. Enter the **CalDAV calendar address** or **CalDAV task address** as the full address of the
   collection.
3. **Check access**: Mailhelp checks in read-only mode whether the address is a calendar collection and accepts the
   matching entry type.
title: CalDAV and Apple Reminders

text: A changed target applies to new Proposals. Proposals already displayed remain bound to the target for which they were created; after a target switch, Mailhelp locks their creation and requires a new confirmation. A target profile can only be removed when no Mailbox uses it anymore. Instructions for assignment: [Manage accounts](Konten-verwalten.md).
title: Switch target safely

text:
Review date: November 11, 2026. This is a review of the setup instructions against official
documents; no real accounts were connected and no external entries were created.

- Google: [Calendar permissions](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/auth)
  and [OAuth including refresh token expiration](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2).
- Google Tasks (November 16, 2026): [Task resource with date limit and field lengths](https://developers.google.com/workspace/tasks/reference/rest/v1/tasks)
  as well as [List with pages and done tasks](https://developers.google.com/workspace/tasks/reference/rest/v1/tasks/list)
  and [read existing task lists](https://developers.google.com/workspace/tasks/reference/rest/v1/tasklists/list).
- Notion (November 16, 2026): [API version 2026-03-11](https://developers.notion.com/reference/versioning),
  [Create page in a data source](https://developers.notion.com/reference/post-page),
  [Query data source](https://developers.notion.com/reference/query-a-data-source) and
  [Error codes](https://developers.notion.com/reference/status-codes).
- Todoist: [personal API token and API](https://developer.todoist.com/).
- Microsoft: [Device code sign-in](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/v2-oauth2-device-code)
  and [Graph permissions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/permissions-reference).
- CalDAV using Nextcloud as an example: [Collection address and app password with two-factor protection](https://docs.nextcloud.com/server/latest/user_manual/en/groupware/sync_windows10.html).
- Apple: [App passwords](https://support.apple.com/en-gb/102654) and
  [Change of iCloud Reminders](https://support.apple.com/en-us/102457).
  Mailhelp uses the existing CalDAV/VTODO adapter; this does not imply support
  for the new iCloud Reminders lists. This limitation remains explicitly in place.
title: Verified provider sources

text:
Tested for Mailhelp 7.0. What to do in everyday operation: review and decide on Proposals, read Mails,
answer follow-up questions, and track the State of entries.
title: Everyday operation

text:
**Open** shows all proposals that need a decision. Each card names kind (task
or event), title, times, target and the evidence from the email. On large screens the
list is on the left and the selected proposal on the right; the `A` key creates the selected proposal.
The **Source evidence** (the email with attachments) is expanded immediately from 1024 px width, on
narrower screens initially collapsed; its heading names the sender and number of images.

Above the list are the quick filters and below them search, sort order and grouping.
The search finds proposal titles, subject and sender. The number in the heading then reads
something like “4 of 12”. The sort order offers “Newest email first” (default, by receipt at
Mailhelp), “Oldest email first” and “Next event / next deadline first”; entries without a date
are at the end. “Group by what is needed” divides into “Question needed”, “Ready to
confirm” and “Further check needed”. All settings are in the address and remain on
reload; “Reset” shows everything again. The bar only changes the display.

| Button | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **Add as task** / **Add to calendar** | creates exactly this version immediately (no undo) |
| **Dismiss** | no creation |
| **Already done** | mark as done, no creation |
| **Send answer** | answers a question or changes fields (“Title: …”, “Location: …”) |
| **End editing** | discards a started change |
| **Repeat duplicate check** | after a failed check for existing entries |
| **Create again** | only after a question, if the same entry was already created earlier |

The bottom navigation remains on the phone even when scrolling at the visible
screen edge. The safe distance to the Home indicator remains clear. Via “More”
among other things Status and Settings can be reached.
title: Open decisions

text:
On release, the final finger position counts. Pulled to the right or left beyond the threshold, it triggers the displayed action; normal scrolling and a swipe canceled by the browser send nothing.

On a smartphone and tablet, you swipe right to create an Event or a Task, and left to Dismiss a suggestion. The card follows your finger even diagonally. **To the right** creates (or “Relevant”), **to the left** dismisses (or “Irrelevant”). Below the card are the icon and wording of the action. From about 40 % of the card width, it is triggered on release. A short, fast swipe is also enough if it covers at least half the distance and continues in the same direction. Steeper pulling continues scrolling the list; a swipe from the screen edge remains reserved for the system gesture.

Without triggering, the card springs back. When triggered, it flies to a narrow Result strip. This shows “Processing …” and is replaced by the server result. If the server rejects, the card returns with the error message. If the response is interrupted, the status check remains active; Mailhelp sends nothing again.

If a suggestion first needs clarification, a lock appears on the right. There the card moves like a rubber band; on release, a hint states the reason. Dismissing remains possible. Unsent text blocks both directions until you send the reply or empty the field. Input fields and horizontally scrolling areas keep their controls. A normal tap on the title, link, or button still works. Mouse and wide screens from 1024 px do not use the gesture.

On first visit, a fully visible, decidable card moves gently once after a short pause. This does not trigger an action. The line below explains the directions. “×” (Close hint) or the first successful swipe ends both on this device; a hint already closed earlier remains closed. With “Reduce motion” in the system, there is no demonstration, tilt, or flight animation. The card still follows the finger directly. Without JavaScript, the forms and buttons remain the complete operating path.

On the phone, you read the title and sender/Time before the actions. The numbers for “Open decisions” and “Open” update after the decision, even with set filters. After the last decision, “All done” appears. Filter chips fading to the right can be pushed further sideways; the active filter is kept visible when opening. Explanations about relevance can be found under “What do these decisions mean?”.
title: Swiping on the phone

text:
For changes or cancellations of an existing event, the button is called **Update existing
event** or **Cancel event**. If a change matches multiple events, you use “This event means: …” to select the right one.

If another email brings different fields for the same event or the same task, the follow-up question names both values and their origin, for example “Contradiction for the end time:
previously 16:30, according to email “Parents' evening” from 08.11. 19:30. Which end time should apply?”.
Both values are shown side by side on the card. A button such as “Keep 18:30”
or “Take 20:30” sets the value with one click and creates a new version; it is only created once you confirm this
version. For a completely different value, you change the suggestion or reply freely.
In Telegram, the same values appear in the message and as buttons below.
title: Follow-up questions and contradictions

path: Video link for an existing event
text:
If an online event is already in the calendar without a dial-in link and a later email provides the link, Mailhelp does not create a second event. The card shows “Update existing event: add video link” with the link; only **Update existing event** writes it into the description of the existing event. Title, times, attendees and your notes stay unchanged.
If the event already has a different conference link, Mailhelp asks which one applies; the old link is only replaced after your choice and confirmation. If the same link is already there, the proposal stays “Already exists”. Only addresses of known providers such as Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet or Webex count as conference links, not registration or organiser pages.

A proposal that an older version already closed as existing although it contains a link offers **Compare with calendar again**. This compares the link with the current calendar and creates at most a new version, which you confirm separately.
title: Video link for an existing event

text:
If Mailhelp holds two Proposals for the same thing or an Email brings additional Fields for an existing Proposal, you decide in the **Proposal review** (`/abgleich`):

- **Add to this entry:** Adds the Fields from one Proposal to the existing entry. No second entry is created; you then confirm the supplemented Proposal under Open.
- **Keep as a separate proposal:** Both remain separate Proposals under Open.
- **Adopt permanent acceptance:** Remembers a fixed assignment rule for future Proposals.

If Mailhelp has submitted the assignment itself for review, the recommended button is highlighted.
title: Proposal review

text:
Mailhelp retrieves every written entry fresh from the provider:

| Display | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Saved – entry being verified | written, verification retrieval running |
| Created and verified | the provider shows the entry with the confirmed fields |
| Entry not yet confirmed | not findable or retrieval not possible; the reason is stated |
| Entry present, fields differ | Table “Confirmed / At the provider” |
| Calendar file provided – transfer to the calendar not verifiable | file sent via Telegram |

**Check again** reads only once more; Mailhelp never changes, repairs, or repeats a
creation.
title: After creation

text:
If you accidentally confirmed a suggestion or the occasion no longer applies, you can delete the entry from the calendar or task list again within a deadline (by default 10 minutes after creation, configurable via `targets.removal_window_minutes`):

- **Web interface:** On the result card (“Your action”) and on the suggestion detail page, the **Remove entry again** button appears during the deadline. It leads to a confirmation page that shows title, time and target. With **Really remove entry**, the entry is deleted at the provider; **Cancel** returns without changes. After the deadline expires, the direct link to the provider (“Open in calendar” or “Open task”) appears instead.
- **Telegram:** Under the message “✅ Created …”, the **Remove again** button appears. A click asks for confirmation (“Really remove: …?” with “Yes, remove” and **Cancel**).
- **Security:** If the entry at the provider has meanwhile been changed manually (e.g. by a family member), Mailhelp refuses deletion in order to protect third-party changes.
- **History:** A removed suggestion is marked in the History and under “Recently done” as **Removed again** and does not count as accepted in the acceptance rate.
title: Remove created entries again

text:
**Mails** lists all processed Mails. The email page shows “This is how this email was processed” with each stage and its result. If Mailhelp overlooked something, **Task or Event overlooked?** starts a targeted re-analysis (**Analyze again**, limited by a daily limit). You take new findings with **Take result** as unconfirmed proposals; **Cancel re-analysis** ends a running one.

In **History** you find every change and decision with its version. You can filter by terms, Status and Kind, under **More filters** also by Event and Time range.
title: Read Mails and History

text:
The learning mode helps set up topics and filters: Mailhelp reads a selection of existing
Mails, classifies them freely and suggests topics, exclusion topics, senders to ignore
and additional retrieval folders from them. It only reads: The mailbox is not changed, and no
Events or Tasks are created. Only what you explicitly confirm is applied.

All learning functions are under **Learning** (`/lernen`). The learning overview shows three cards with
purpose, current state and metrics: **Learn from Mailbox** (the learning run below),
**Learn from decisions** (improve rules from your previous decisions, see
[Learn from decisions](#aus-entscheidungen-lernen)) and **Proposals** (measure acceptance rate by Kind, topic and sender, see [Measure and improve acceptance rate](#annahmequote-messen-und-verbessern)). Opening the overview or a
card starts nothing and costs nothing. The topics themselves are managed under Settings → Topics.
title: Learning mode (learning function)

path: Start learning run in the web interface
text:
1. In the navigation under **Administration**, open the **Learning** page (`/lernen`) and
   select “Open learning from mailbox” (`/lernen/postfach`). The overview does not start anything.
2. Under **New learning run**, in the “1. Mailbox and folders” stage, select the **Mailbox** and
   select **Load folders**. Check the saved folders of this mailbox; additional
   folders are possible under **Additional folders (one name per line)**. Loading does not start
   a mail retrieval and works without JavaScript. In the “2. Scope” stage, specify the
   **Number of mails** (1–1000, preset 20).
3. In the “3. Costs and budget” stage, specify **Price cap USD per million tokens** and **Budget USD**. The price cap is
   your assumption; check current model prices including output and reasoning yourself.
4. Select **Show estimate**. Mailhelp states the typical estimate and the worst
   case in tokens and USD. If the budget is not sufficient, the required minimum amount is shown there.
   Mailbox, folders, number, price, and budget remain in the form. The listed
   models come from the configuration; the price cap remains your manual assumption.
5. Select **Start read-only learning run (chargeable)**. For 20 mails, depending on the model,
   a budget of about 1 USD is typically sufficient.

During the run, the page shows “Running: … mails checked, … errors”. You control it with **Pause**,
**Resume**, and **Cancel**. The budget is checked before every AI call;
the run stops before it would be exceeded. If the configuration has been changed since the start,
the run cannot be resumed; a new learning run replaces it.
title: Start learning run in the web interface

text:
In a customer instance run by an operator (customer mode, from 8.7.4) the learning run counts in
points instead of money. The operator sets prices, tokens and models; you do not see them.

1. Choose mailbox, folders and number as above. In the “3. Points limit” stage, enter the
   **Points limit for this run** (a whole number from 1 to 10,000,000). The limit is not a credit
   balance but the ceiling of this one run.
2. Select **Show estimate**. Mailhelp states the estimated usage and the worst case in points.
   If the limit is not sufficient, the required minimum number of points is shown there.
3. Select **Start read-only learning run (uses points)**. If the operator changes the valuation
   between estimate and start, the start is refused; show the estimate again.

During the run the page shows reserved and actually used points; calls whose cost is not known yet
are counted and named. The run stops before it would exceed the limit. After the adoption, new
topics apply from the next analysis and new fetch folders from the next start; you do not need to
reload anything. The “Usage” page also shows the usage under “Learn from mailbox”. If
the operator has not set up learning yet, the page says so and offers no start.
title: Learning in a customer instance

text:
After the run, **Topics, exclusions and evidence** show per suggestion the title, description, the
evidence from the Mails and the senders:

- **Takeover:** **Do not take**, **Topic** (relevant, `topics.yaml`) or **Exclusion topic**
   (irrelevant, `irrelevant_topics.yaml`).
- **For all mailboxes** takes the topic globally instead of only for the selected mailbox.
- **Ignore senders for exclusion topic** additionally sets the senders for an exclusion topic
   to the list of ignored senders (`irrelevant-senders.json`).
- **Save selection as draft** remembers the decision per suggestion.

Under **Additional retrieval folders** you select folders that will also be retrieved in the future
(**Save folder selection**). Only **Explicitly take selected topics, filters and folders**
writes everything together into the configuration; **Dismiss** discards the result.
Afterwards select **Reload configuration** so that email retrieval uses the new topics.
title: Check and take result

path: Learning Mode in the Terminal and Settings
text:
Alternatively, the learning mode runs interactively in the terminal. This command reads 20 Mails and prompts for the topics one after another:

```sh
mailhelp --learn 20 --mailbox 1 --config-directory .
```

With multiple mailboxes, `--mailbox NUMMER` or `--mailbox alle` is required. In Docker, `compose.learn.yaml` with writable configuration is provided for this.

Under **Settings → AI and Statistics**, `learning.parallel_llm_calls` (simultaneous AI calls in learning mode, default 4) and `learning.decision_llm_content` are available for this.
title: Learning Mode in the Terminal and Settings

text: Regardless of the learning mode, Mailhelp stores every manual decision about a suggestion with Email, AI results, original and decided suggestion in the learning data (`data/<Betriebsart>/learning/decisions.jsonl`). It is the material for [Learning from decisions](#aus-entscheidungen-lernen); Mailhelp does not thereby change its topics or decisions independently, but only after your approval and confirmation. Complete AI requests and responses are added only with `learning.decision_llm_content`. Retention is governed by `retention.decision_learning_days` (default unlimited).
title: Learning data

text:
You can find rule learning under Learning: choose “Open learning from decisions”
(`/lernen/entscheidungen`). The
topic management (Settings → Topics) also links to this page. This function uses the
decisions already logged; it does not retrieve any Mails. The function requires the
prompt block `decision_rule_learning` in `prompts.yaml`. For older installations, take the block
from the supplied example and reload the prompt configuration as usual.

1. Under “Which decisions?” choose: **Only new decisions since the last analysis**
   (default, at most 100) or **All previous usable decisions** (at most 500,
   more evidence and higher costs). The current count is shown behind each option. If there are no
   new ones, choose “All previous”. Read the note about data transfer and possible costs. Choose only after checking the
   explicit approval “Analyze decisions”. Limited excerpts and
   corrections are transmitted to the active AI provider. Without approval, no call is made.
2. After completion, read the summary at the top; the links jump to the individual
   Proposals. It also states how many similar rejections were sent to the AI
   only as a count. In each card, “Previous rule and proposal” shows only the changed fields;
   new and removed examples are marked with “+ new” and “− removed”, unchanged fields
   are opened by “Show unchanged fields”. “Decision evidence” lists Subject, Decision and Date; the
   excerpt opens with “Show excerpt”. A rejected Task does not automatically make
   its Email irrelevant; “already done” remains a positive example.
3. Change name, Description, examples, exclusions and activation as needed. Examples
   and exclusions are listed individually, one per line. Existing topic IDs and mailbox areas remain
   stable. Optionally, under “Edit complete topic YAML (optional)”, enter a complete
   topic; this then replaces the field values.
4. In each card, under “Decision on this proposal”, choose **Apply**, **Dismiss – do not
   propose again** or **Leave open** (default). The bar at the bottom counts
   how many are applied and how many are dismissed. Choose **Review selected changes**. The separate
   comparison **Review edited changes** shows exactly your field or YAML changes.
   Only there, check **Explicitly confirm selected rule changes** and
   choose **Apply reviewed changes**. “Continue editing” opens editing;
   then review again. A new review state replaces the previous one. Without a selection or
   with invalid YAML/schema, nothing is applied. The entries remain for correction. For externally
   changed files, resolve the conflict and start a new analysis of the current state.
5. For “Analysis failed”, the cause is shown below. After “truncated at output
   limit”, Mailhelp has already made a second, reduced attempt. Try again later
   or choose “Only new decisions”. The AI log shows the token usage and length of the truncated response for this.
6. For interrupted writing after login, explicitly confirm “Complete application”.
   Mailhelp checks all files again and completes only the already approved local
   change. It does not start a new AI call and does not overwrite third-party changes.
7. The review view lists dismissed Proposals under “Will be dismissed and not proposed
   again”. If only Proposals are dismissed, the button is called **Dismiss proposals**;
   no rule file is changed. “Leave open” saves nothing – a later run may bring the
   proposal again. At the bottom of the page, “Show previously dismissed proposals” lists all
   blocked Proposals with Date and change; **Allow again** lifts the block.
   During the next analysis, Mailhelp tells the AI which changes you rejected. If
   it still proposes the same change, Mailhelp hides it; the summary states how many
   Proposals were hidden this way. The AI may nevertheless bring a differently worded rule with the same meaning again – then simply dismiss it again.

New analyses apply relevant rules at the next safe processing point. The
exclusion topics keep their previous meaning in learning/decision test mode; for
normal mail analyses, the relevant topics and their exclusions apply. Existing
Calendar entries and Tasks are not changed by rule learning. A new analysis
replaces a still open review draft; a restart does not repeat a running AI analysis.
title: Learning from decisions

path: Measure and improve the acceptance rate
text:
Under **Learning → Proposals** (`/lernen/vorschlaege`), Mailhelp measures how many proposals you accept and how many you dismiss. The Statistics help you identify where incorrect proposals arise and how to avoid them in a targeted way.

1. **Metrics and Statistics:** Three tiles show the overall acceptance rate, for Tasks and for Events. Below them follow the history per calendar week, sortable tables by topic and by sender, and a breakdown of dismissal reasons. The time range can be filtered via the dropdown (e.g. 30, 90 days or Entire time range).
2. **Reasons for dismissals:** After dismissing a proposal (on the web on the result card or in Telegram), Mailhelp optionally asks “Dismissed. Why?”. Five fixed reasons are available: “Does not concern me”, “For information only”, “Advertising or newsletter”, “Misrecognised (date, content)” and “Other reason”. The field is never mandatory; Dismiss remains a single step. One click saves the reason, which flows into Statistics and as a feature into rule learning.
3. **Sender notices:** If a sender causes a conspicuously high number of incorrect proposals (at least 5 decided proposals in 90 days with an acceptance rate of no more than 10%), a notice appears on the Statistics page and the result card. “View” opens a preview of all stored Mails from this sender with accepted proposals marked. By pressing a button, the Address can be added to the sender prefilter after explicit confirmation. “Do not suggest again” hides the notice; previously dismissed notices can be allowed again at any time in the overview.
4. **Notice about rule learning run:** If at least 20 new dismissals have occurred since the last rule learning run, Mailhelp recommends a new learning run at the top of “Open” and “Learning” in order to refine your topic rules. The notice appears at most once per week and can be paused for seven days with “Hide”.
title: Measure and improve the acceptance rate

text:
Under **Settings → Sender rules** (`/einstellungen/absender`) you specify which Mails Mailhelp classifies already before every AI call. As of 7.7, there are three kinds:

- **Ignore:** Mails are classified as irrelevant without an AI call and without notification – for an Address (`newsletter@shop.de`), a Domain with all subdomains (`shop.de`), a Pattern with `*` (`no-reply@*`), or a Subject (`Automatische Antwort:`).
- **VIP – always relevant:** Mails count as relevant without a relevance check, even if a block matches. The Events and Tasks from them still require your confirmation; a VIP only saves the relevance check.
- **Exception only:** lifts any block for a sender without making them a VIP. Previous Mailbox Exceptions are listed here and can be converted with “Make VIP”.

You first check a new rule with **Check matches**: Mailhelp counts how many of the last 200 Mails it would have matched, and warns for Domains of large email providers. Only then does **Save rule** appear. Each rule shows matches and last match and can be switched off and on again.

On an Email you find next to the sender **Ignore sender**, “Ignore domain …” (with the name of the Domain) and **Mark as VIP**. If Telegram asks whether an Email is relevant, the button 🚫 **Always ignore sender** ignores the sender in future; **Undo** only removes this rule again. Which rule classified an Email is shown under “How this Email was processed”.

The **Header prefilter** detects automatic system Mails (`Auto-Submitted`, `Precedence`) and newsletters (`List-Id`, `List-Unsubscribe`). Both filters are initially off. In the **Trial**, the AI still decides; Mailhelp only counts how many Mails would have been filtered out. Circulars that you want to keep, you enter as a **Distribution list exception** (e.g. `<eltern.schule.de>`).

**Learning → Proposals** suggests new rules from your decisions: senders whose Mails the AI repeatedly classified as irrelevant, and senders whose Mails always led to confirmed Proposals. **Statistics** shows in the “Prefilter” section how many relevance checks were omitted, and estimates the savings from the real checks in the same Time range.
title: Sender rules and prefilter

text:
On the phone, only the Quick filters are at the top; **Search and sort** expands Search, Sort order and grouping. The bar at the bottom leads to **Open**, **Mails**, **Review** and **History**; **Status** and the remaining areas are under **More**.

On phone and tablet, you can decide cards with swipe gestures (see [Swiping on the phone](#wischen-auf-dem-telefon)).
title: Operation on the phone

text:
The “English” or “Deutsch” link at the end of the navigation changes the interface language for
this browser. The language cookie retains the choice for one year. Without a saved choice, Mailhelp
uses the supported browser language with the highest quality weight, then `language` from
`config.yaml`. The web interface, Help, JavaScript messages and offline pages support both languages.
Original emails and user-written text retain their wording. Normal email analysis continues to use
the configured prompts; changing language does not start another analysis.

Open `/de/` or `/en/` to choose the demo language before starting. Both corpora contain 30 synthetic
emails and proposals ready for confirmation. Switching language changes the interface and retains
your decisions and current corpus. A confirmed restart loads the corpus in the selected language.
Restart requires confirmation, affects only your session and invalidates previous forms.

`mailhelp --language en --help` shows English CLI help without configuration or service access.
`--language` applies to the individual invocation and can also be used with `--demo`.
title: Language

text:
If a connected service refuses the sign-in, a notice “Connection problems” appears above **Open** and **Emails**. It names the service and mailbox or target profile, the effect (for example “Calendar sync and calendar changes are not possible at the moment.”), the time of the last failed check and the link **Check connection** to the matching settings page. Mailhelp does not claim “expired” when the service only reports a refusal.

The notice stays visible with filters, reloads and restarts and cannot be dismissed. It disappears only once the same service has been reached successfully again; saving new credentials alone is not enough. An open page shows new notices and their removal after at most 15 seconds. Timeouts and network errors do not count as sign-in problems. Mailhelp checks connected services read-only at start and then every 15 minutes.
title: Connection problems

text:
In a hosted Inboxstride instance you connect Google Calendar without client data or tokens of your own. In the initial setup (step “Calendar and tasks”) and under **Settings → Target profiles**, **Connect with Google** leads to Google. There you choose your account and allow calendar access. Back at Inboxstride you continue with **Choose calendar**, pick a calendar with write access and confirm with **Adopt connection**. Only then does the new connection apply; until then a previous one stays unchanged, also after a cancellation or an error. Like every connection change it takes effect only after you run **Check connections** in the setup and then apply the settings; if the check is missing, the setup says so.

The connection itself creates no events. When the account changes, open proposals of this profile need a new confirmation. If Google later refuses the access, the “Connection problems” notice leads straight to **Reconnect Google**. Google Tasks remains reserved for self-hosting with an own Google client.

Once a connection exists, the same page offers **Choose another calendar**: Inboxstride reads the calendars with write access through the existing access, without a new Google sign-in, and **Adopt calendar** saves the choice. **Disconnect** stops issuing tokens for this profile at once, also for an access still cached. Events already created stay, other profiles stay connected, and the grant at Google itself is not revoked; you can do that in the security settings of your Google account if needed. Afterwards **Reconnect Google** leads to a new connection.
title: Connecting Google through Inboxstride

text:
The Status page shows under “Recent errors and action required” which Email is being retried or has been given up. **Failed emails** opens the error list (`/mails?state=failed`): Each row states cause, processing stage, and number of failed attempts and offers **Try again**, **Ignore**, and **Details** directly; after the action you return to the list and see the result. **Try again** starts the continuation at the next retrieval and resets the previous attempts; until then the Email appears in the list as “Retry requested”. **Ignore** (called File until 7.3) ends it as not processed and files it away; the Email remains in the archive and disappears from the error list.

On the Email page, an error appears at the very top in the “Processing errors” section with stage, cause, recommendation, state of retry, and the same buttons. **Show error report** expands all details: timestamps, field paths, and model call IDs. **Copy report** places the report as text in the clipboard, for example for troubleshooting; it contains no Email text, no addresses, and no access data. In the error list, **Details** opens the same report as a dialog.

Above the error list are **Try all again** and **Ignore all**. A confirmation page first states the number of affected Mails; only there is the action triggered. Afterwards the list reports how many Mails were queued. Mails that have changed in the meantime or are already queued are skipped. “Try all again” omits Mails without analysis data and already requested retries. Both buttons only change the stored state. A new Event or a Task still requires its own confirmation of the suggestion.
title: Failed Mails

text:
The chat icon at the bottom right opens **Settings Help** as a small window over the current Settings page. “Ask about this” adopts the reference for a setting without overwriting an existing question draft. Enter a question and select **Send question**. The answer first appears in short form; **Show detailed answer** displays all steps.
While the answer is being generated, you can search, edit Values, and confirm and save changes. The chat remains open; answers do not reload the Settings page.

Sources open in the window; **Back to conversation** returns to the same place in the History. Even after changing pages, reloading, or reopening, the conversation remains at the last-read position; if you read at the very bottom, you see new answers automatically. Drag the header (or focus the title and use the arrow keys) to reveal hidden Settings. Drag at an edge or corner for more space (by keyboard, Shift+Arrow keys on the title); the size is retained when changing pages.
**Close help chat** hides the window. When reopened, the conversation and draft are still present as long as the session and retention apply. **Clear chat** discards the contents and keeps the window open. Mailhelp automatically saves the unsent question as you type; without JavaScript, new answers appear on the next page load. The chat only explains and does not itself change any data.
title: Help with Settings

text:
Lists (history, emails and analytics) have a toolbar at the top: search and the main selectors share a row with the primary action. Additional filters are under **More filters**, together with the number currently active. **Reset** appears when a filter is applied. Filters are included in the address, so bookmarks retain them.
Emails, history and proposal matching show one row per item: title, sender and time, with a status badge on the right. Click the title to open the email or proposal.

| Page | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| **History** | Every change and decision with its version; filter by search, status and type, or by event and period under **More filters** |
| **Briefing** | Daily overview of open decisions and events |
| **Topics** | What counts as relevant (Settings → Topics): overview, search and editing with a preview |
| **Learning** | Learn from the mailbox and improve rules using decisions |
| **Analytics** | Costs, durations and charts of AI calls |
| **Status** | Last contact with each service and current stage; click a metric to open the corresponding overview |

On **Status**, click one of the four metrics to open its entries. **Open proposals** and **Relevance questions** lead to separate overviews with details for each proposal or email. **Failed emails** opens the email archive with the failed filter. **Queued web actions** shows the queue with links to your individual actions. Other sessions are listed without private content. The overview remains accessible with zero entries. “Refresh overview” loads the latest state; opening or refreshing it does not execute any action.
Below this is the number of emails Mailhelp has fully processed so far, including irrelevant and duplicate emails. Telegram `/status` starts with the same number. An email is briefly excluded from the count while it is being analysed again.
title: Page overview

text:
At the top, the key figures are shown as tiles; a click opens the matching calls. The links above them jump to charts, flow, and the table “By model and stage”. On the phone, the charts are collapsed (**History and Distribution** opens them). If no calls were recorded in the time range, only a note is shown there.

**Statistics** shows costs and times of the AI calls for the selected time range. Durations appear in the matching unit, for example `4 Min. 12 s`, `20 Std. 54 Min.` or `3 Tage 4 Std.`; for the summed call duration, the exact seconds are shown in parentheses after it. The summed call duration adds all attempts, including parallel ones, and is not an end-to-end time.

The cost chart shows a dashed average line and, from 14 days, a 7-day average. The **Call duration** is a scatter plot: each point is a call, crosses are errors, the line is the median per day. **Compute time per processing stage** states the share and duration of each stage; the **email processing flow** shows all stages in their order and marks the longest waiting time; local stages are called “local · not measured”.

Every Value in the fact table is a link. It opens the call list with the matching preset, for example only the failed calls with their cause, the most expensive, or the longest. Status and sort order can be changed there; “← Back to Statistics” retains the filter. Individual calls are available only for the retention period of the metrics (default 90 days).

Mailhelp measures every processing stage, not only the AI calls. The fact table states the **end-to-end time per email** (without the time in which an email waits for your decision; this is shown below). “Time per processing stage” shows how much time each stage actually takes; the flow plan states duration and AI share for each stage (“of which AI”) and marks the longest waiting time. “Preparation in detail” divides preparation into parsing, attachments, and image recognition. A click on a stage under “Slowest runs” shows the slowest emails of this stage. On **Status**, for the running stage, it states how long it usually takes.

Mailhelp only places reply drafts in the Drafts folder; it never sends emails.
title: Statistics

text:
The Settings show nine check levels for the signed-in device. On iOS, open Mailhelp from the Home screen as an installed web app via HTTPS. Turn on Server Push under Setup, enter a valid VAPID contact and restart. Then activate the device. Missing Mailbox channels can be added after an explicit, version-checked preview.

A test push transmits exclusively a fixed neutral type. Provider acceptance and device feedback are separate states; the visible system message must be checked on the device. After a key change or 401/403, reactivate. 429, 5xx and network errors remain repeatable. Own changes and Proposals open before activation do not generate a new push. Save subscriptions, VAPID, activation times and version origin in the persistent data directory. Details: [Release 6.8](../archiv/Release-6.8.md).
title: Web Push from 6.8.1

text:
Reviewed for Mailhelp 8.1. Safe next steps for common problems. None of these steps creates duplicate entries: Mailhelp never repeats a write whose outcome is unclear; it reconciles it with the provider first.

For contradictory event revisions, `answer_revision_failed` includes the content-free
`revision_contract`: `known_clock_changed`, `known_facts_changed`, `known_facts_lost`
or `revision_conflict`. These distinguish changed clocks, changed/lost temporal facts
and other conflicts without logging the answer. A code alone never authorizes recovery:
check the current version and stored normalized answer, then use the read-only
preflight described in [Operation](Betrieb.md).

| Situation | Cause | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mailbox sign-in failed | Incorrect username, password or connection type | Check **Settings → Credentials**; use an app password with two-factor authentication; **Check access** |
| Folder missing | Folder name differs from the server | Use the discovered folder list on the mailbox page |
| Google sign-in expired (`token_refresh_denied` in the log) | Refresh token revoked or expired | Run **Connect Google** again |
| Microsoft sign-in refused | Token expired | **Connect Microsoft** or `mailhelp --microsoft-login` |
| Provider unreachable | Network problem or provider outage | Wait; Mailhelp retries. **Status** shows the last contact |
| AI budget exhausted | `limits.llm_calls_per_minute` reached | No action needed: the email will be analysed automatically later |
| “The message exceeds a safety limit” | Email too large or deeply nested | Raise the `limits` only for trusted emails |
| Setting “saved – takes effect after a restart” | Not active yet | **Settings → Restart Mailhelp** |
| Creation not yet verified | Entry not visible at the provider or read access refused | Inspect the entry at the provider, then **Check again** |
| Unclear write outcome | Provider response was lost | No action needed: Mailhelp reconciles and does not create the entry again |
| Target changed, creation blocked | Proposal confirmed for a different target | Restore the original target or confirm the new proposal |
| “Shutdown not performed” or “Restart not performed” | Confirmation belongs to an earlier startup or is incomplete | Confirm again on the same page; if that fails, stop Mailhelp in its terminal with Ctrl+C |
| “Mailhelp is already running …” | Second startup using the same data directory | Stop the running instance |
| Forgotten web password | – | On the host, run `mailhelp --reset-web-password --config-directory .` |
title: Troubleshooting

text:
The status page lists affected emails with the start time, stage, attempt count and next attempt. “Abandoned” means Mailhelp has suspended automatic processing. Open the email and fix the cause first. “Retry” resets the attempt count and waiting period. “Ignore” deliberately ends processing; the email stays visible in the archive as unprocessed and no longer counts as requiring attention.
This cannot restore analysis data already removed; in that case only Ignore is available. Both actions are also available directly in the error list (`/mails?state=failed`). Neither creates events or tasks.
title: Email repeatedly fails to process

text: “Action detection cannot be resumed – analysis data removed by retention” means a completed email has a failed action-detection stage whose required analysis results have since been removed. Mailhelp ends automatic resumption once, with `resume_abandoned`. The email remains visible in the archive under the failed filter. If you want it analysed again, explicitly start a reanalysis.

text:
1. Stop the running service cleanly; the reset command requires exclusive access to the data directory.
2. On the host, run `mailhelp --reset-web-password --config-directory .` in the configuration directory. This deletes the existing password hash and signs out all web sessions; it does not generate a new password.
3. While the service is stopped, run `mailhelp --pair --config-directory .` and keep the one-time terminal code ready. Restart the service and sign in with this code.
4. After successful sign-in, explicitly set a new web password at `/einstellungen/web-passwort` if desired. Never enter the code or password in the help chat.
title: Resetting the web password

text: **Settings → Check connections** tests each connection without writing and gives a result and recommended action per service. **Check everything (self-test)** on the same page tests all components. path: Help chat in the settings window
text:
The window stays open while searching or saving. If it is in the way, drag its header, or focus the title and use the arrow keys. Only **Close help chat** hides it; **Clear chat** removes the conversation. If an answer does not appear, reload the page. Do not resend a question because you changed pages: Mailhelp shows the existing job.

If browser storage is blocked, Mailhelp saves the window state on the local server before navigation. If that fails, the page retains the draft; check your connection and try again. Without JavaScript, an unsent question is not retained when changing pages. If “crypto.randomUUID is not a function” appears (Mailhelp over `http://` on the home network before 5.5), update to 5.5; since then Mailhelp can generate keys without a secure context. Sign in again after logout or session expiry; a new session does not inherit old private chat data from browser state.
title: Help chat in the settings window

text:
For one paused date/time clarification fixed in 8.1: stop the application and make
a consistent private backup. Check the mail ID, proposal ID, current version,
answered question and stored normalized answer, including an unambiguous four-digit
year. Run `python -m devtools.recover_revision --data data/production --mail <mail-id> --proposal <proposal-id> --version <version> --timezone Europe/Berlin`
using the actual data path and configured timezone. The default is read-only preflight.
Only after successful preflight, repeat with `--apply`. The tool rechecks version and
state under lock and requeues just this answer without a model call or external action.
Restart and verify exactly one successor version, the correct local start and the
remaining end question. Never reset all paused answers. On failure keep it paused;
restore the consistent backup only while stopped and before new processing, without
overwriting newer write evidence. Ask the user for the missing end; never guess it.

Mailhelp tries the same failure for an email at most five times. The intervals are 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes and 2 hours. After that, the email remains stored and is no longer picked up automatically. Permanent errors are abandoned immediately. Provider rate limits apply only their own waiting period. Status shows the stage, start, attempt count and next attempt. Telegram reports abandonment once, with a link to the email if the web interface is enabled.

`logging.verbose: false` reduces routine lines: unchanged folder counts hourly, one completion per Telegram poll, and web requests only on errors or when taking over a second. The first stack trace stays complete; repeats appear every 15 minutes with a counter. “Verbose log” enables individual messages after a restart; full LLM contents still require their own switches. The synthetic daily limit is 2 MB with unchanged rotation limits.

New state files contain optional retry fields. Before returning to an older version, these must be removed compatibly from the current state. Never blindly replace later confirmed write outcomes with an old backup.
title: Recurring processing errors

text:
| Command or page | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `mailhelp --check --config-directory .` | Validates configuration without network access |
| `mailhelp --check-access --config-directory .` | Checks all access without writing |
| `mailhelp --config-directory .` | Starts the service |
| **Settings → Restart Mailhelp** | Controlled restart; saved changes take effect |
| **Settings → Stop Mailhelp** | Stops the service |

Only one instance runs per data directory. **Reload configuration** changes connections without restarting the process.
title: Starting, checking and stopping

text:
| Step | What happens | When it takes effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Save | After the preview (“Review”), a changed setting is written to `config.yaml`. The page says “saved” until it takes effect. | – |
| Apply during operation | Mailhelp automatically applies settings such as polling intervals, retention, metrics, personal information, notifications, event durations, proposal matching, drafts and briefings. | At the next safe point, without a restart |
| Activate | Mailboxes, IServ accounts and target profiles are saved as drafts on their pages and activated only after another explicit confirmation (**Apply draft**, **Check connection and activate mailbox**). | Between two mailbox cycles |
| Reload configuration | **Explicitly reload configuration** applies topics, prompts, mailboxes, credentials and target profiles after unfinished analyses are complete. | At the next safe point, without restarting the process |
| Restart | **Restart Mailhelp** shuts down the service cleanly and starts it again; all other saved settings, web access and data-directory changes take effect. | Immediately after the restart |

Saving or activating never creates tasks or events; that always requires explicit confirmation of a proposal.
title: Saving, activating, reloading and restarting

text:
`mailhelp --demo --config-directory <leeres Verzeichnis>` starts a demo with 30 prepared sample emails, without a mailbox, Telegram, AI or real targets. Each visitor gets a private copy for two hours through “Start demo”; confirmations are simulated only. Port and hostnames: `MAILHELP_DEMO_PORT`, `MAILHELP_DEMO_HOST`, `MAILHELP_DEMO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. The demo refuses directories belonging to normal installations, and vice versa.

Starts are limited to 5 per client and 60 overall per hour. Behind your own reverse proxy, set `MAILHELP_DEMO_TRUST_PROXY=1` so the client address comes from `X-Forwarded-For` (last entry; the proxy must append its peer address, as nginx, Caddy and Traefik do). Do not set the variable without a proxy, or visitors could bypass the limit with an invented header. Visitors answer clarification questions only with prepared example answers and reset their own copy through “Restart demo”. The demo automatically removes expired copies.
title: Demo instance

text:
```sh
MAILHELP_DEMO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=demo.example.org docker compose -f compose.demo.yaml up -d --build
```

`compose.demo.yaml` starts the same image entry point with `--demo` and a separate `demo-daten` volume. It does not mount the normal instance’s `.env`, `config.yaml`, data or logs. Both instances run independently, including simultaneously. The `mailhelp-demo` network is internal, so the container cannot reach the internet. This is the second protective layer: the demo does not construct clients for mailboxes, Telegram, AI or targets in the first place.

The HTTPS proxy for the demo subdomain joins `mailhelp-demo` and forwards to `mailhelp-demo:8765`. An internal network cannot publish a port on the host. If the proxy runs on the host (for example Tailscale Serve), the service needs a normal network with `127.0.0.1:<Port>:8765`; a firewall rule for the demo network then blocks outbound traffic (on Linux in the `DOCKER-USER` chain). Keep `MAILHELP_DEMO_TRUST_PROXY` set only while the proxy is the container’s sole point of access.

To reset the entire demo, stop its container and delete the `demo-daten` volume. At the next startup the directory is empty and receives a new marker.
title: Demo in a Docker container

path: Language entry points behind the proxy (verified on 18 Nov 2026 with 7.8.1)
text:
Since 7.8.1, Mailhelp serves `/de/`, `/en/` and `/sprache?wert=de|en` itself. The answer is a redirect (303) to the start page with the cookie `mailhelp_lang` (`Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, one year); an invalid value returns 400. The proxy therefore passes these paths through unchanged and sets neither a language cookie nor a redirect of its own.

Switching an existing proxy configuration:

1. Check at the container without the proxy that `/en/` answers 303 with `Set-Cookie: mailhelp_lang=en`.
2. Back up the configuration file of the demo subdomain.
3. Remove the mappings for the language cookie and the cache header, the two `add_header` lines for them and the blocks `location = /de/` and `location = /en/`.
4. Run `nginx -t` and only on success `systemctl reload nginx`; otherwise restore the backup.
5. Check over HTTPS: `/en/` with a German browser shows the English start page, `/de/` with an English browser the German one; a demo start shows the matching sample data.

Way back: copy the backed-up file back, `nginx -t`, `systemctl reload nginx`. Versions before 7.8.1 need the proxy redirect because they do not know `/de/` and `/en/`.
title: Language entry points behind the proxy (verified on 18 Nov 2026 with 7.8.1)

path: Server update with an image (verified on 18 Nov 2026, 7.7.6 → 7.8.1)
text:
The productive instance and the demo run as Compose projects of the same image. The update ran as follows:

1. Create a source archive of one commit: `git archive <commit> Dockerfile README.md pyproject.toml requirements.lock src`; on the server, unpack it into its own release directory `<version>-<commit>` and build the image `mailhelp-production:<version>-<commit>` from it.
2. Check the version in the image without network: `docker run --rm --network none --entrypoint python <image> -c "import mailhelp; print(mailhelp.__version__)"`.
3. Back up both Compose files, replace image and build path in them and check them with `docker compose config --quiet`.
4. Stop both containers (production with a 45-second grace period), only then archive the runtime directories of both instances; this gives a consistent state.
5. Start both containers without rebuilding, wait for the health checks and check the version in the running container. If a step fails, the backed-up Compose files are written back and the previous containers are started again.

Result on 18 Nov 2026: both health checks passed, version 7.8.1 in both containers, existing demo visitors were taken over without errors. Way back: copy the backed-up Compose files back, restore the backed-up runtime archives with the containers stopped and start the containers with the previous image, which is still present. Credentials stay in the instance's `.env` and are taken over neither into the source archive nor into the image.

Observation after the restart: Google refused to renew the calendar access (HTTP 400) because the refresh token of an OAuth app in the Google status `Testing` expires after seven days. The remedy is a new Google sign-in through the web interface; switching the app to the Google status `In production` helps permanently.
title: Server update with an image (verified on 18 Nov 2026, 7.7.6 → 7.8.1)

text:
For a consistent backup, stop the service cleanly first. Copy the files only after it has fully stopped, then start Mailhelp again.

Back up `config.yaml`, `.env`, `prompts.yaml`, topic files, the data directory (`data_directory`, readable JSON state files) and, if needed, the log directory. `.env` contains credentials and must be kept private.
title: Backups

text:
Restart the service after installing a new version. Stylesheets and scripts are read at startup. Each page references the correct content hash for every file, even when an older service worker handles the initial request.

1. Stop Mailhelp. This is mandatory on Windows, which otherwise locks the executable.
2. Back up configuration, `.env`, prompts, topics and the data directory (see Backups).
3. Fetch the new version and install it in the same virtual environment: `python -m pip install -r requirements.lock` and `python -m pip install --no-deps -e .`.
4. Run `mailhelp --check --config-directory .`, then start the service.

New settings use their defaults without rewriting your `config.yaml`. New prompt stages are not silently inserted into a custom `prompts.yaml`; the corresponding release report explains how to adopt them.
title: Updating
